title: Drought development characteristics modulate global dry–wet abrupt alternation through distinct land–atmosphere feedbacks
content: This study shows that antecedent drought development is linked to distinct, region-dependent pathways from drought to extreme precipitation, providing a basis for anticipating compound hydrological extremes. Rapid transitions from drought to extreme precipitation can trigger cascading impacts, but the influence of antecedent drought development on subsequent precipitation remains unclear. Dry–wet abrupt alternation events were identified using a global event-scale framework and separated into successive dry and wet phases.
